prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a target protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase so that the cell destroys it, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type degraders.

statement.case_for: I keep B014 as my preferred single-part prize. The scientific principle is new: a small molecule does not occupy a site but induces proximity between a ligase and a target, and catalytic, event-driven removal follows. That reaches proteins with no conventional pocket. The principle has been reproduced independently for two decades, and the chemistry (E3 ligand choice, linker design, ternary-complex cooperativity) is firmly chemical. The round-1 exchange sharpened one point for me. The chair asks whether the missing approved PROTAC is a reason to defer. I do not think so, because the thalidomide-type glue drugs are approved and Handa's cereblon work is exactly what shows that the induced-proximity mechanism is clinically real, so the clinical objection is answered for the principle if not yet for every PROTAC. Crews and Deshaies give the concept and first demonstrations, and Handa gives the mechanism of the clinically proven strand. Three names is the most that fits, and this is the trio that keeps one citation honest about what it covers.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and round 1 did not remove it. Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim all have serious claims, and Ito's omission beside Handa is uncomfortable because the cereblon identification was a joint paper. The citation has to be written so that it does not claim to cover the whole field. The members who treat PROTACs and glues as two achievements may be right, and I cannot show that they are not. If the committee cannot accept this cut, the failure is one of credit and not of science, and then I would turn to B046, whose two-name credit is clean, before anything else.

responses.point: Chabes chooses Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned PROTACs into a rational design discipline, and that the cereblon strand is a separate molecular-glue lineage.
responses.response: Chabes makes the best case for Ciulli and I take it seriously: the structural work is what made degrader design rational, and I do not rate it below Handa's on scientific quality. I still hold Handa, for two reasons. The cereblon mechanism explains why a drug class used for decades works, so it supplies the clinical proof that B014 otherwise lacks, and it is the one strand that connects PROTACs to molecular glues in a single mechanistic frame. A PROTAC-only citation naming Ciulli would leave the approved drugs outside the prize and would strengthen the argument that the field is premature. I would move to Ciulli only if the committee decides the citation should be restricted to heterobifunctional degraders; I do not yet see that as the stronger reading.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N coupling on mechanistic clarity and daily use, and admits the 2010 prize and the precursor work of Kosugi and Migita leave a novelty and credit question.
responses.response: I agree with Brzezinski that the mechanism is well understood and that two names is a clean allocation, which is why I moved B046 to my first alternative. Answering the chair's question, though, I cannot yet write one citation sentence that separates it from the 2010 prize without saying it is a ligand-controlled extension of the same catalytic cycle to a new nucleophile. That is a real advance in synthesis but a smaller conceptual step than a new pharmacological principle. The cost of B014 is open attribution and the cost of B046 is overlap with a recognised idea, and I weigh the second as the harder to fix by wording.

responses.point: Somfai argues that excluding Kosugi on generality grounds is defensible and that the committee should say so openly, and that C-N coupling is a clear conceptual advance through ligand control of each catalytic step.
responses.response: The generality argument for excluding Kosugi is sound and Somfai is right that it must be stated in the open. I will use the same standard on my own choice. Applying it, Crews and Deshaies established the concept and Handa the cereblon mechanism, while Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto extended it afterwards. I find that more defensible than the reverse, but I accept that the same sort of exclusion argument is harder for B014 because the lineages overlap in time. If Somfai and Brzezinski can show in round 2 that a C-N citation clearly names a concept beyond 2010, I would regard B046 as a fully acceptable outcome and not only a fallback.

responses.point: Linke asks whether there is appetite for a third computational prize after 2013 and 2024, and prefers Car-Parrinello for its unambiguous two-author credit and four decades of use.
responses.response: The merit and credit of B027 are not in doubt, and I said so in round 1. My reservation is unchanged: two computational prizes in about a decade make a third hard to justify next to a candidate with a new modality. I also hold the view that this is my own field and that I should discount any preference of mine there, so I keep B027 as a second alternative and not as a lead position. I would not rank it above both B014 and B046.

responses.point: Sparr prefers Cullis, Hope and Madden for ionizable lipid nanoparticles, arguing that the lipid phase-behaviour chemistry is rigorous and that clinical validation is at large scale, while admitting credit is spread over at least six people.
responses.response: The pKa-controlled charge and non-bilayer phase behaviour for endosomal escape is sound physical chemistry, and I accept that the clinical evidence is wide. What keeps me from B060 is the same difficulty as in B014 but worse: Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan are left out with strong claims, patent disputes cloud priority, and the 2023 Medicine prize makes delivery look to some like an optimisation after the principle was rewarded. I need that one citation to carry a single new chemical idea, and for B014 I can state it more directly.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies, and whether a citation can be honest about leaving out Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim.
Whether the committee will accept that approved cereblon glue drugs answer the maturity objection for the PROTAC strand, or will insist on an approved PROTAC.
Whether C-N coupling (B046) can be set apart from the 2010 prize in one sentence; if it can, my ranking of it would rise.
Whether the committee will treat PROTACs and glues as one achievement or two.
statement.conflict_note: I was a postdoc with Arieh Warshel (2013 laureate, EVB), and B027 lies in my own field of computational chemistry, so any view of mine on it should be discounted. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to any credited name in B014 or B046, and I declare no recusal. This is unchanged from round 1.
